definitions.explanation: A thin slice of tissue, material, or specimen prepared for examination under a microscope. Standard terminology in biology, medicine, and materials science.
The point where a line or curve crosses an axis on a graph. In the equation y = mx + b, the value b is the y-intercept.

notes:
Compound of {切|せつ} ('cut') and {片|へん} ('piece; fragment'). The word covers two distinct technical domains: biology/medicine (thin slices for microscopy) and mathematics (axis intercepts).

USAGE:
In biology and medicine (sense 1), {切片|せっぺん} refers specifically to prepared specimens. The process of making sections is called {切片|せっぺん}⟦{作製|さくせい}→作製：04187_sakusei⟧. In mathematics (sense 2), {切片|せっぺん} usually appears with an axis label: y{切片|せっぺん} or x{切片|せっぺん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{凍結|とうけつ}→凍結：09613_touketsu⟧{切片|せっぺん}: frozen section
- {薄|うす}{切片|せっぺん}: thin section
- {切片|せっぺん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{染色|せんしょく}→染色：15817_senshoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to stain a section
- y{切片|せっぺん}: y-intercept
- x{切片|せっぺん}: x-intercept

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{断片|だんぺん}→断片：10915_danpen⟧: fragment — a piece broken off from something; not prepared or sliced intentionally
- ⟦{断面|だんめん}→断面：21317_danmen⟧: cross-section — the surface revealed when something is cut through; focuses on the exposed surface rather than the slice itself
- ⟦{標本|ひょうほん}→標本：13174_hyouhon⟧: specimen — a broader term for any sample prepared for study
